title: Atom-aware Protein Representation Learning Improves Protein Structure Prediction
claim: Multi-view discrete tokenization feeds a generator-discriminator corruption-and-recovery pretraining scheme that learns joint representations.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, curved arrow linking tokenization to pretraining
description: The figure has two rounded gray panels. The left panel, titled 'Atom-level Tokenization' in blue, shows two white cards with 3D protein renderings. One is a yellow ribbon backbone and the other is a gray protein with red side-chain atoms. Each card feeds into a blue trapezoid tokenizer (Backbone Tokenizer, Sidechain Tokenizer), which outputs a row of colored tokens: orange for backbone and dark red for full-atom. The right panel, titled 'Pretraining', shows a stack of three token rows (full-atom in red, backbone in orange, sequence in gray). Some entries are dashed blanks. These rows go into a Generator Model made of an embedding layer and transformer layers. The generator outputs rows with hatched corrupted tokens. A thick blue curved arrow carries these rows into a taller Representation Model, a stack of transformer layers on an embedding layer. That model predicts the original tokens in a 'Masked Token Prediction' row at the top right. Color coding by view carries through the whole figure.
caption: TRIPROREP. (a) Three-view tokenization. A protein is independently tokenized into amino-acid, backbone, and full-atom token sequences at the residue level. (b) ELECTRA-style discriminative pretraining. A small generator corrupts each of the three sequences, and a large discriminator predicts the original token at every position.
abstract: Recent advances in generative modeling show that pretrained representations can improve generation as conditioning features or alignment targets. Motivated by this, we study protein representations for predicting structures beyond conventional function annotation. We propose TriProRep, a structure-aware pretraining method that jointly models three aligned residue-level views: amino-acid identity, backbone geometry, and local full-atom geometry, discretely encoded via VQ-VAE tokenizers. By pretraining to recover original tokens from generator-corrupted views, TriProRep learns to distinguish plausible but incorrect cross-view augmentations from the original protein. We further introduce RepSP, a benchmark for evaluating protein representations in structure-predictive settings. RepSP tests three uses of representations: homodimer co-folding from apo-chain representations, residue-level prediction of homodimer-derived interaction properties, and representation-aligned monomer structure prediction. Across these tasks, TriProRep improves over sequence-only and prior structure-aware representation models, while maintaining competitive performance on conventional benchmarks.
